description:
crates.io has kopi-beans 0.1.2 (2026-08-07) through 0.1.7 (2026-08-13). This repo's crates/kopi-beans/Cargo.toml still says version = 0.1.1, and the last commit touching crates/kopi-beans/ is 5f55124 dated 2026-07-27. So roughly three weeks of kopi-beans work exists ONLY in the published crate and was never committed here.

Measured: unpacked kopi-beans-0.1.7.crate and diffed its src/ against repo HEAD's crates/kopi-beans/src/. 53 entries differ; 3373 added lines in the published tree vs 902 lines only in ours. Direction is unambiguous -- the published tree is ahead. Sample: cli_surface/commands/ready.rs in 0.1.7 emits "run bn blocked" where the repo still emits the pre-fork "run bd blocked". Also src/bin/tailnet_proxy.rs (repo) was renamed to src/bin/bn_tailnet_proxy.rs (published).

Consequences:
1. git is not the source of truth for kopi-beans. The published binary our own dogfooding rule tells us to run is not the code in this repo.
2. Publishing from this tree is impossible as-is -- 0.1.1 is already taken.
3. Anyone reading crates/kopi-beans/ to understand bn's behaviour is reading three-week-old code. That already cost time this session: gh-68 was diagnosed against in-tree code, and it only held because compat/export.rs happens to be byte-identical between repo HEAD and 0.1.7.

NOT auto-reconciled: which tree is authoritative is the maintainer's call, and a 53-file merge done blind could silently drop either side's work. Needs a decision first.

Suggested resolution: recover the tree the 0.1.7 publish was made from (the machine that ran cargo publish still has it; failing that the unpacked .crate is a usable floor), commit it as a single "import kopi-beans 0.1.2..0.1.7 published work" commit, then rebase the in-tree-only changes (the gh-68 fix in 84d3f6b) on top and bump to 0.1.8.
title: kopi-beans: repo source is 6 published versions behind crates.io (0.1.1 in-tree vs 0.1.7 released)
